content.text: Section 11 is on point and sec-10 contains no early-deletion trigger. This meets or exceeds the preferred position.

input.quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. ... 11.2 Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position on every material term: (a) up to six months of transition assistance at Customer's request, priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form (more favourable to us than "then-current rates") and expressly including knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier and continued service at existing scope and service levels; (b) return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, with no fee-dispute withholding right; and (c) secure deletion with written officer certification. Critically, deletion under 11.3 is sequenced to occur only "After Customer confirms successful return," so there is no risk of Customer Data being destroyed before we have retrieved it, and the carve-out for a legally required copy is limited by ongoing protection and use restrictions. Section 10 does not undercut this: 10.1 ends access only "after any agreed transition period" and preserves our rights in Customer Data, and 10.2 adds delivery of Deliverables plus refunds of prepaid Fees. No redline needed.
